harnesses.notes: Mimir writes the file-based managed tier. An MDM profile for com.anthropic.claudecode ranks above the file and, with the default managedSourcesBehavior 'first-wins', hides Mimir's file completely. Deploy settings for Claude Code through Mimir only. Since v2.1.242, setting managedSourcesBehavior to 'merge' in the highest-ranked source (the MDM profile) makes Claude Code compose every admin source instead of hiding lower ones — an org that wants both an MDM profile and Mimir's file applied must opt in there, not in Mimir's file. Claude Code also reads a managed-settings.d/*.json drop-in directory alongside managed-settings.json; Mimir does not write into that directory yet. CONFIRMED this review (raw fetch): drop-in files merge alphabetically after managed-settings.json — plain scalars last-file-wins, lists union+dedupe, nested blocks merge key-by-key, but fallbackModel, managedMcpServers, extraKnownMarketplaces and modelPicker are replaced whole by the later file rather than merged. Also confirmed: the allowedProviders cross-source merge now requires Claude Code >= v2.1.285 to take effect. No new top-level mergeRule keys found this review beyond the ones already modeled below. Docs also reference several more keys (allowedChannelPlugins, channelsEnabled, disableCommandPluginSources, parentSettingsBehavior, policyHelper, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, crossSessionInbound, enableArtifact) whose exact types/semantics were not pinned down with a quote this review — left out of mergeRules pending a follow-up pass that confirms their types (see PR 'Unverified').

outputs.description: Managed settings (highest file-based precedence; users cannot override).

harnesses.notes: Claude Desktop only reads the com.anthropic.claudefordesktop managed-preferences domain; there is no file-based alternative. Mimir writes that plist in /Library/Managed Preferences directly, which Apple does not document for third parties: macOS may remove it when profiles change, and Mimir restores it within seconds. Do not also deploy a vendor profile for this domain. Claude Desktop reads policy at launch; users must restart the app. CONFIRMED this review via two direct raw fetches of https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration: the plist is documented as read PER-USER, literally '/Library/Managed Preferences/<user>/com.anthropic.claudefordesktop.plist', not the single device-wide path Mimir currently writes and this entry's output models — Mimir needs to write (or additionally write) the per-user path before this policy is reliably read; see PR 'Needs Mimir change'. Same raw fetch confirmed exact types for several more keys, added below: builtinBrowserAllowedDomains, sshHostAllowlist and coworkEgressAllowedHosts are string[] restriction allowlists; blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories and disableBypassPermissionsMode are boolean kill switches; disabledBuiltinTools is a string[] deny list; builtinToolPolicy is a per-tool allow/ask/blocked map. Two more confirmed keys were left out as not policy-relevant: organizationInstructions (free-text model guidance, not an enforced control) and inferenceModels (overrides the auto-discovered model list wholesale, not a restriction). requireCoworkFullVmSandbox is now marked Deprecated in the vendor table with no replacement key confirmed yet — kept here since deprecated keys typically still function during a migration window; recheck next review. Docs also note a 2026-10-07 migration cutoff after which several renamed/legacy key forms fail closed (not catalog-relevant directly, but explains default-behavior changes for anyone still on old key names).

outputs.description: Enterprise policy keys for Claude Desktop.

harnesses.notes: Mimir writes the system managed config, which overrides global, project and remote (.well-known/opencode) config. An MDM profile for ai.opencode.managed also overrides everything and conflicts with Mimir's output. Full precedence (lowest to highest), confirmed against the opencode source: remote (.well-known/opencode) < global < OPENCODE_CONFIG < project < .opencode/ dirs < OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT < Mimir's managed file dir < the ai.opencode.managed mobileconfig. opencode has no per-MCP-server allow/deny list; governance is only via remote-provided servers with a per-server enabled toggle. The 'strictest' ordering used below for share/permission.* is Mimir's own more-restrictive-wins policy choice, not a vendor-documented cross-source merge rule — opencode's own docs only describe plain tier override.

outputs.description: Managed opencode.json (keys: mcp, permission, provider, model, disabled_providers, enabled_providers, share, autoupdate, …).

harnesses.notes: requirements.toml holds hard constraints users cannot change (deployed locally or via an MDM profile for com.openai.codex using the requirements_toml_base64 key); managed_config.toml holds managed defaults the user can still override at runtime (MDM key config_toml_base64). Precedence is requirements.toml > cloud-managed configuration defaults (ChatGPT Business/Enterprise) > managed_config.toml. CORRECTED this review (confirmed against the codex-rs source): allowed_sandbox_modes is NOT deprecated, it is still a live, actively-tested requirements.toml field alongside allowed_permission_profiles, where any profile omitted from the list (including future built-ins) is denied. managed_config.toml itself is the one being phased out — Codex's own source calls it a 'best effort' legacy layer being replaced by requirements.toml, and it is already fully removed on Windows. Codex's own internal cross-source composition for the allowed_* fields is actually last-layer-wins override, not intersect; the 'intersect' strategy below is a deliberate Mimir-side policy choice (stricter than Codex's native default) layered on top of that, not a mirror of vendor behavior.

outputs.description: Legacy/deprecated managed defaults layered above the user's config.toml (approval_policy, sandbox_mode, otel telemetry block, check_for_update_on_startup, …); OpenAI is phasing this file out in favor of requirements.toml and has already removed it on Windows.

harnesses.notes: CONFIRMED device-level mechanism (re-verified this review against the raw docs in google-gemini/gemini-cli), genuine candidate for 'supported'. Casing confirmed exact: system overrides at /Library/Application Support/GeminiCli/settings.json, defaults at system-defaults.json in the same folder (env override: GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH). Precedence System overrides > Workspace > User > System defaults (arrays/objects merge rather than replace). Keys: tools.core (array, tool/command allowlist -> union), tools.sandbox (string enforce e.g. 'docker'), mcp.allowed (confirmed true allow-list, intersect: 'a server must be permitted by every source to run') + mcpServers (canonical server defs, union-by-name, System > Workspace > User on name collisions), telemetry.enabled / telemetry.logPrompts (bool kill switches -> anyFalse), privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled (bool -> anyFalse), security.disableYoloMode (bool lock -> anyTrue), security.auth.enforcedType (string, last/admin wins). excludeTools/tools.exclude is now deprecated in favor of policy-engine deny rules. The TOML policy engine ([[rule]] with toolName/decision/priority, plus richer fields subagent/mcpName/toolAnnotations/commandRegex/modes/denyMessage) loaded from Admin dirs (/Library/Application Support/GeminiCli/policies on macOS) uses a 5-tier priority system (Default=1, Extension=2, Workspace=3 [currently non-functional, see gemini-cli#18186], User=4, Admin=5); Admin always outranks the others. The admin policy directory is ignored entirely if it isn't root-owned and non-group/other-writable — Mimir must write it with those exact permissions. Recommend promoting to supported.

CHANGED since last review: a genuine on-device mechanism now exists (GA 2026-07-01, extended to CLI/VS Code 2026-07-08) making this a strong candidate for 'supported'. Two device-level channels, both read by Copilot CLI: (1) native MDM managed preferences for the com.github.copilot domain (macOS profile, string values only with dot-separated nested keys and JSON-encoded arrays/objects; Windows equivalent HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\GitHubCopilot); (2) file-based deployment at /Library/Application Support/GitHubCopilot/managed-settings.json on macOS (/etc/github-copilot/managed-settings.json on Linux, no native MDM on Linux) - file must be owned by root, not group/world-writable, no symlinks; client restart required to reload. Precedence: MDM-managed > server-managed (org's copilot/managed-settings.json in .github-private, legacy path .github/copilot/settings.json) > file-based > user's own ~/.copilot/config.json — EXCEPT sandbox and permissions.deny/ask/allow, which vendor docs say are composed in the most restrictive direction across delivery methods regardless of this precedence. Keys, re-confirmed directly from github/docs source this review: allowedMcpServers is vendor-documented, verbatim, as intersect ('a server must be permitted by every source to run'); permissions.allow is likewise documented as intersect, not union — same non-obvious stricter-than-expected pattern; deniedMcpServers and permissions.deny/ask are union, deny always wins; permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode is a string enum ('disable'/'unmanaged'), not a boolean, but still anyTrue-shaped (any source setting 'disable' wins); model (string, top-level key now supersedes legacy permissions.model, last/highest-precedence layer wins); enabledPlugins (union); extraKnownMarketplaces/strictKnownMarketplaces (most-restrictive wins). NEW this review (CLI 1.0.93, 2026-10-07, confirmed from the official changelog.md): permissions.limitTo — a network-domain allowlist ('enforce managed domain boundaries for network requests'; only Domain(...) entries valid, an empty list denies all) that sits alongside permissions.allow/deny/ask with deny still winning — same restriction-allowlist family as allowedMcpServers, so intersect. Carried-forward open research items (key names not yet pinned to an exact quote): autoTier, remoteControl, a richer telemetry object, features.computerUse, an {"overridable": value} wrapper, an 'Assisted Permissions' kill switch and a minimum-CLI-version key referenced in changelog 1.0.94 (2026-10-08) but not yet confirmed by exact JSON key name. Caveat still open: GitHub issue github/copilot-cli#4959 (managed 'model' key not reliably applied in non-interactive CLI runs) re-confirmed OPEN as of 2026-10-12 (desktop app v1.1.25 bug confirmed Oct 1, triaged Oct 5, no maintainer fix yet) — this still blocks promoting to 'supported'. Recommend promoting to supported once that CLI bug is fixed, or shipping the file-based /Library/Application Support/GitHubCopilot/managed-settings.json output now with a note about the interactive-only model-key caveat.

CHANGED since last review: cursor.com/docs/enterprise/deployment-patterns now documents a genuine device-level mechanism — a macOS .mobileconfig configuration profile (a reference profile for the current bundle ID, com.todesktop.230313mzl4w4u92, ships inside Cursor.app's own Resources), deployable via Jamf/Kandji/Intune or by hand. Documented keys include AllowedExtensions, AllowedTeamId, WorkspaceTrustEnabled, UpdateMode, NetworkDisableHttp2 and ExtensionGalleryServiceUrl, each overriding user/workspace settings outright (no union semantics documented at this layer). CORRECTED this review: the MCP allow-list surface actually has two paths, not one — ~/.cursor/permissions.json (user) AND <workspace>/.cursor/permissions.json (per-repo) — and vendor docs describe them as concatenated/combined across scopes (mcpAllowlist -> union), not override; either can also be dropped in place by MDM at the device level. CAUTION added this review: cursor.com remains unreachable for a direct fetch (every attempt — apex, docs subdomain, .md variants — failed again); a Cursor-staff forum reply (forum.cursor.com, June 2026) says the real .mobileconfig profile schema only supports AllowedExtensions/AllowedTeamId/ExtensionGalleryServiceUrl/UpdateMode, casting doubt on whether WorkspaceTrustEnabled and NetworkDisableHttp2 are genuine profile keys versus marketing copy — not changed in this catalog pending a direct-fetch confirmation, but flagged here and in the PR. Multiple October 2026 forum bug reports also claim the permissions.json user+repo merge/wildcard matching is broken in practice. Candidate for 'supported' once the full key list and merge semantics inside the shipped .mobileconfig are read directly from a live environment.

RESOLVED this review (direct source reads of microsoft/vscode-docs and github/docs): the long-open precedence question between VS Code's native chat.* policy and GitHub's com.github.copilot managed-settings layer is now answered by a new page, docs/enterprise/manage-ai-settings.md (dated 2026-10-07): 'If both systems configure the same control, the enterprise-managed setting takes precedence. The values are not merged.' Full cross-channel order: MDM-managed settings > server-managed settings > file-based settings > user settings, EXCEPT permissions.deny/ask/allow and sandbox, which are composed in the most restrictive direction across all of them regardless of that order. github/docs' enterprise-managed-settings.md and deploy-managed-settings.md also give the full VS Code-supported key table for GitHub's own com.github.copilot domain: permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode (kill switch), permissions.allow (intersect)/deny/ask (union, deny wins), allowedMcpServers (intersect)/deniedMcpServers (union, deny wins), sandbox (limit, requires VS Code Agent Host >= 1.138.0), telemetry, model/autoTier (enum). Separately, VS Code's own native com.microsoft.VSCode policy surface (policies.md, re-fetched) grew since last review: new keys include ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization, ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly, ChatPluginsEnabled/ChatEnabledPlugins/ChatExtraMarketplaces/ChatStrictMarketplaces, Claude3PIntegration, Codex3PIntegration, 8 CopilotOtel* telemetry keys, McpEnterpriseManagedAuthIdp, BrowserChatTools, ChatDefaultModel, and several Dictation* keys, alongside the previously-catalogued ChatAllowedMcpServers/ChatDeniedMcpServers/ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly/ChatAgentSandboxEnabled-etc./TelemetryLevel/EnableFeedback/ExtensionsAutoUpdateDelay/ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations/UpdateMode/ExtensionsAutoUpdate. com.microsoft.VSCodeInsiders remains a separate, still-unconfirmed domain. With both the full key list and the cross-layer precedence now confirmed from official sources, this is a strong 'supported' candidate — see PR 'Candidates for supported'. No output added yet: the mechanism is a native MDM managed-preferences domain (plist), and /Library/Managed Preferences/com.microsoft.VSCode.plist is not yet in Mimir's path allowlist — see PR 'Needs Mimir change'.

CHANGED since last review: Cognition rebranded Windsurf to Devin Desktop on 2026-06-02 (same app, same com.exafunction.windsurf bundle ID kept for compatibility); canonical docs moved to docs.devin.ai/desktop/enterprise-policies, which docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/enterprise-policies still mirrors. That page confirms a device-level mechanism: a macOS .mobileconfig configuration profile, with a sample shipped inside the app bundle, deployable via MDM or by hand — separate from VS Code's own policy surface. Search snippets suggest keys for an MCP server allowlist, a managed-MCP-only lock, and telemetry/feedback toggles, but this run could not fetch the live page directly (egress-blocked) to confirm exact key names/types, so no mergeRules are added yet. Needs one direct read of docs.devin.ai/desktop/enterprise-policies before promoting to 'supported'.

Only user-level YAML config (~/.config/goose/config.yaml), plus sibling permission.yaml/secrets.yaml. Needs a YAML writer and a per-user output mode. New this review (confirmed against the official repo's docs source): an admin MCP/extension allowlist exists via the GOOSE_ALLOWLIST env var, pointed at a YAML file (hosted anywhere, edit-access-restricted) listing permitted extensions ({id, command}); if unset, no restriction applies. It is a restriction allowlist (intersect-shaped) but is delivered via an externally-hosted file referenced by an env var, not a local device file Mimir can write directly — still not a 'supported' candidate, but no longer 'no admin mechanism at all'.

Enterprise policy is delivered via Cline's remote/cloud config, not a device file; not a 'supported' candidate. CONFIRMED this review via WebSearch-quoted text from docs.cline.bot (still blocked for a direct fetch): remote-config keys include mcpMarketplaceEnabled, allowedMCPServers, remoteMCPServers, blockPersonalRemoteMCPServers and the previously-noted yoloModeAllowed kill switch, all cloud-delivered. Also confirmed: Cline now ships a standalone CLI (separate from the VS Code extension) that stores its own data under ~/.cline/data/, with MCP settings at ~/.cline/data/settings/cline_mcp_settings.json (overridable via the CLINE_DIR env var) — a different path from the VS Code extension's globalStorage path already in detect below. Added the CLI path as an additional discovery hint; no admin mechanism writes to either path.

Could not find a credible, maintained official project under this exact name this review. The most-referenced same-named repos appear to be repo-squatting/SEO-spam or parody projects (one self-describes as 'an agent-managed museum exhibit' with implausible star counts, explicitly disclaims affiliation, and tells users it has been renamed to a different project, 'agent-code'). No official vendor site, docs, or maintained GitHub org could be confirmed. Leaving this entry as-is (no outputs, no documentation link) rather than encode any detail from a low-trust source; a future review should check whether 'agent-code' or another canonical name is the real successor.

CORRECTED again this review: a French-locale kiro.dev page (kiro.dev itself remains unreachable in English for a direct raw fetch) describes a real local managed-policy file — /Library/Application Support/Kiro/managed-settings.json — deployable via Jamf/Kandji and applying to 'every Kiro surface on the machine' including the CLI, with a restart required to reload; this supersedes last review's dev.kiro.desktop/auto-updater-only conclusion for general CLI policy, though it should still be re-confirmed from an English-language primary source. Documented rule semantics: the admin layer can only set deny/ask (never allow), and deny/ask always win regardless of scope — a good match for Mimir's restrictive-wins default. User-level policy lives at ~/.kiro/settings/permissions.yaml (deny/ask/allow), alongside the existing per-user CLI settings at ~/.kiro/settings/cli.json. Kiro CLI remains AWS's rebrand of Amazon Q Developer CLI; the exact rebrand date is still unconfirmed from a primary source. This is a strong 'supported' candidate once re-confirmed directly, but /Library/Application Support/Kiro/ is not yet in Mimir's compiled-in path allowlist, so no output is added here — see PR 'Needs Mimir change'.

Terminal coding agent from Factory AI; installed via install script, Homebrew cask (droid) or npm. Settings at ~/.factory/settings.json with a ~/.factory/settings.local.json override and a project-level .factory/settings.local.json. A 4-level settings hierarchy (Org > Folder > Project > User), each level a .factory/ folder with its own settings.json, covers model policy, network restrictions and autonomy ceilings — org level is admin-owned and highest-priority. CONFIRMED this review (WebSearch snippets, docs.factory.ai still blocked for a direct fetch): a key named maxAutonomyLevel is an org-level hard cap that clamps the user's own autonomyLevel even if the user sets it higher (limit/kill-switch style), and command allow/deny lists 'accumulate across levels' rather than override. This still reads as org/cloud-distributed configuration (synced from a cloud endpoint), not a macOS-device/MDM-dropped local file — still not a 'supported' candidate. Needs a direct fetch of docs.factory.ai before adding outputs or mergeRules.

Terminal coding agent from Sourcegraph; npm package @ampcode/cli (formerly @sourcegraph/amp, still supported), now a single-file Bun-compiled executable. Global config at ~/.config/amp/settings.json/.jsonc; workspace .amp/settings.json overrides it (searched upward to repo root, workspace > user except keymaps). A genuine OS-level managed-settings file is documented: macOS /Library/Application Support/ampcode/managed-settings.json (Linux /etc/ampcode/managed-settings.json, Windows C:\ProgramData\ampcode\managed-settings.json), same schema as user settings and able to 'override any other Amp setting.' CONFIRMED this review via WebSearch-quoted text from https://ampcode.com/news/enterprise-managed-settings and https://ampcode.com/docs/cli/settings (ampcode.com itself is still unreachable for a direct fetch): amp.mcpServers is a grant list (union); amp.mcpPermissions is a first-match-wins ordered rule list matching MCP servers by url (remote) or command/args (local), defaulting to allow when nothing matches — a restriction mechanism where rule order matters, so a straight union is not quite right; amp.permissions is a similar first-match-wins rule list for Bash command patterns. Precise managed-settings-vs-workspace precedence is still only strongly implied ('override any other setting'), not stated as an explicit ordered list — recommend one more direct-fetch pass to pin that down before adding mergeRules. This remains a strong 'supported' candidate, but /Library/Application Support/ampcode/ is not yet in Mimir's compiled-in path allowlist, so no output is added here — see PR 'Needs Mimir change'.

Native macOS terminal with a built-in Agent Mode. User settings live in ~/.warp/settings.toml (TOML, not JSON). Enterprise policy (agent autonomy, model allowlists, secret redaction, sharing) is enforced through a cloud-based Admin Panel for teams, not a macOS device-level MDM profile or managed-preferences domain — not a managed-config candidate until an on-device mechanism is documented; policy-managed settings are shown greyed-out in the app but pushed from the cloud, not a local file. CONFIRMED this review via WebSearch-quoted text from Warp's own file-locations doc (docs.warp.dev still blocked for a direct fetch): the macOS app bundle ID for the Stable build is dev.warp.Warp-Stable, previously only a third-party-sourced guess — added to detect below.

New entry. Meta's coding agent CLI (beta 2026-08-05, GA 2026-08-31), running on the Muse Spark model; installed via a curl install script producing a `muse` binary. Docs reference `muse config validate --plane <defaults|policy>` and a `managed_hooks_path`, suggesting an admin policy mechanism exists, but this run could not confirm an exact macOS managed-config file path/domain from an official source — needs research before adding outputs.

Open-source terminal coding agent (TUI) from Charm; installed via Homebrew (charmbracelet/tap/crush) or npm (@charmland/crush). CORRECTED this review (confirmed via a direct fetch of the repo README): crush.json is now explicitly called legacy/deprecated; the primary config is crushrc, a Bash script with Crush-specific builtins (provider add, model add, permissions allow, mcp add), loaded in priority ./.crushrc > ./crushrc > ~/.config/crush/crushrc. crush.json (schema at charm.land/crush.json) still works but is secondary. Both crushrc and crush.json run as trusted code at load time (crushrc is full shell; $(...) in crush.json executes) — relevant to how much Mimir should trust a project-local config file. No enterprise/MDM mechanism documented — individual-developer tool as of this review.

New entry. Open-source terminal coding agent CLI from the Qwen team, forked from Gemini CLI and optimized for Qwen3-Coder models; codebase search/edit, shell execution and MCP support. Installed via npm (@qwen-code/qwen-code) or Homebrew (qwen-code). No enterprise/admin/managed-config mechanism found in the repo README — needs research, though as a Gemini CLI fork it may eventually inherit a similar mechanism.

New entry. Open-source git-native terminal AI pair-programming CLI that edits repos via model-generated diffs, using tree-sitter/PageRank codebase mapping. Installed via `python -m pip install aider-install && aider-install` (pipx also common). Config file .aider.conf.yml, loaded in priority from the user's home directory, the git repo root, then the current working directory. No enterprise/admin/MDM mechanism found in the fetched docs/README.

New entry. Agentic coding CLI from Augment Code, built on Augment's 'context engine'; analyzes/edits codebases from natural language and integrates with GitHub Actions CI. Installed via npm (@augmentcode/auggie, requires Node.js 22+). Project-level custom commands in .augment/commands/*.md; user-level settings under ~/.augment. No enterprise/admin/MDM mechanism found in the fetched docs — oriented at individual developers and CI.

New entry. Self-hosted 'developer control center' for running coding agents (its own OpenHands agent, or others such as Claude Code/Codex) locally, remotely or in the cloud; formerly known as OpenDevin. Installed via npm (@openhands/agent-canvas) or a Docker image. Offers 'OpenHands Cloud' and 'OpenHands Enterprise' as paid hosted/multi-agent-server products with a self-hosting security-hardening guide, but no macOS device-level/MDM managed-config mechanism was found.
